title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. K is a subfield of C, K̄ its algebraic closure in C, and π1 = Gal(K̄/K). A is the ring of finite adèles of Q. Grothendieck takes a finitely generated tensor category of motives over K. G is the Tannakian group (over Q) of the Betti fibre functor H_B(X) = H(X ⊗_{K} C, Q). He then lists the 'structures' this G carries, labelled by boxes A–G.

[A] The Q-group G itself.

[B] The de Rham side:
- G_K = Aut⊗(H_dR), a K-group.
- P = Isom⊗(H_B ⊗ K, H_dR), a (G_K, G)-bitorsor over K.
- P carries an 'absolute' integrable connection, i.e. a connection relative to Q (Gauss–Manin in the directions of Ω^1_{K/Q}), invariant under G_K.
- This structure is empty if K is algebraic over Q, since Ω^1_{K/Q} = 0.

[C] Over C:
- The comparison isomorphism gives a trivialization α of P_C.
- Transported by α, the base-changed absolute connection becomes d + ω on the trivial torsor, with ω ∈ Ω^1_{C/Q} ⊗_Q g_Q. This is a 'logarithmic derivative of the period matrix', a Maurer–Cartan-type form.
- A second torsor Q_C carries a trivialization β (written β_1).

[D] Hodge-theoretic data:
- Groups G'_K ⊃ H'_K and G''_K ⊃ H''_K, linked by the torsor Q.
- Two cocharacters i1, i2 : G_m → G''_K.
- These are presumably the groups attached to the Hodge filtration / its graded (and a conjugate counterpart), with the Hodge gradings as cocharacters. The exact meaning of each group is not recoverable with certainty from the sketch.
- Grothendieck notes that the complicated datum D can be replaced by the 'subordinate datum' [E], required to be compatible with A, B, C.

[E] The chain G'_K⊗C ≅ G_C ⊃ H'⊗C ≅ H''⊗C ⊂ G''⊗C ≅ G_C. This yields cocharacters i1^C, i2^C : G_{m,C} → G_C, i.e. the Hodge cocharacter μ and its conjugate.

[F] The adelic Galois representation u : π1 → G(A_f), coming from the Betti–étale comparison.

(e) P/G° is a G/G°-torsor over K, pointed by ξ : K → C. It therefore defines v : π1 → (G/G°)(Q).

[G] For each regular connected model S of K of finite type over Z (K finitely generated over Q), with geometric point ξ given by K ⊂ C, there is a topological monodromy w : π1(S(C), ξ) → G(C). This is empty if K is algebraic.

Properties (with comments):
1) i2^C is the complex conjugate of i1^C, so β is determined by α.
2) w factors through G(Q): monodromy preserves the spread-out motivic classes.
3) u factors through π1(S, ξ) for S suitable: good reduction away from finitely many primes.
4) Compatibility squares:
- π1(S(C)) → G(Q) and the profinite completion π1(S) → G(A) commute.
- π1 → G(A) → (G/G°)(A) agrees with v.
- Hence the topological monodromy and the arithmetic component map agree.
5) The composite π1(S) → G(A) → A* is the cyclotomic character. Here ε : G → G_m is the character cut out by the Tate motive ('défini par les racines de l'unité').
6) v is an epimorphism and G/G° is a constant finite group over Q.
7) For each closed point s of S, the image of the Frobenius F_s in G(A) comes from a Q-rational conjugacy class of G. This gives rationality and ℓ-independence of characteristic polynomials ('redonne Weil').
8) G_R equipped with i1^C, i2^C is a 'groupe de Hodge': a reductive real group with Hodge structure, essentially the Deligne-torus homomorphism S → G_R.
9) 'Conjecture Tate': for every ℓ, the image of π1(S) in G(Q_ℓ) acts semisimply on every V⊗Q_ℓ (or on a faithful V), and its Zariski closure is all of G_{Q_ℓ}. The margin says 'devra être précisé'.

Purpose. This is a 1965 axiomatization of what is now called a 'system of realizations' with comparison torsors, packaged around the motivic Galois group. It is a programme for the conjectural properties of motivic Galois groups.
errors: Not an error but a gap: the roles of G'_K, G''_K, H'_K, H''_K and the torsor Q in datum D are only sketched; the text does not make clear which filtration or conjugate fibre functor each represents.

Property 3 should say 'for S suitably small' (an open of a model), as Grothendieck does with 'S convenable'. Property 2 likewise needs S small enough for all motivic classes to spread out. As literally stated 'for every regular model S', w landing in G(Q) may require shrinking S.

Property 9 asks that the Zariski closure equal G_{Q_ℓ} itself, not just its identity component. With 6 this is consistent, but it also presupposes Galois–semisimplicity and the full Tate conjecture over finitely generated fields. Grothendieck flags it as 'devra être précisé'.
Numbering is irregular (5, then 7, 8, 9, with 6 added at the bottom). The item before 8 appears to be 7, overwritten.

ideas.what: Motivic Galois group as Tannakian group of the Betti fibre functor on a finitely generated category of motives over K ⊂ C
ideas.where_published: Only reported via Saavedra's thesis and Récoltes et Semailles (description of motivic Galois group, not these axioms)

ideas.what: De Rham group G_K and Betti–de Rham comparison bitorsor P, trivialized over C by periods
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (period conjecture, cf. footnote in 1966 de Rham paper), Deligne, André, Kontsevich–Zagier
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966) contains the transcendence remark on periods of abelian varieties; torsor formulation unsure

ideas.what: Absolute (relative to Q) integrable Gauss–Manin connection on the period torsor P for K of positive transcendence degree, invariant under G_K, giving a g_Q-valued form ω ∈ Ω^1_{C/Q}⊗g_Q
ideas.modern_name: Gauss–Manin connection over K/Q (Katz–Oda); motivic Galois group with connection / relative period torsor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz–Oda (1968) for the absolute Gauss–Manin connection; André, Ayoub for relative periods and motivic/differential Galois interplay

ideas.what: Hodge cocharacters i1, i2 with i2 = conjugate of i1; G_R a 'groupe de Hodge'
ideas.modern_name: Hodge structure on the motivic group (Deligne torus S → G_R); Mumford–Tate / Hodge group

ideas.what: Adelic Galois representation u : π1 → G(A_f) and its unramifiedness over a model S
ideas.modern_name: Compatible system of ℓ-adic representations valued in the motivic Galois group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (1968 onward; 'Propriétés conjecturales des groupes de Galois motiviques', 1994)

ideas.what: π0(G) is constant over Q and π1 surjects onto it via the torsor P/G°
ideas.modern_name: Component group of the motivic Galois group is a Galois group (Artin motives)

ideas.what: Topological monodromy of a spread-out model lands in G(Q), compatible with the profinite Galois action and with π0
ideas.modern_name: Geometric monodromy inside the motivic/Mumford–Tate group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge II, 1971), André (1992, fixed part theorem)

ideas.what: Frobenius at closed points defines a Q-rational conjugacy class in G (gives Weil-type rationality/independence of ℓ)
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius conjugacy classes in the motivic Galois group

ideas.what: Tate conjecture in Tannakian form: ℓ-adic image is semisimple with Zariski closure G_{Q_ℓ}
ideas.modern_name: Tate conjecture + semisimplicity; with Hodge conjecture implies Mumford–Tate conjecture

ideas.what: Composite with the Tate-motive character is the cyclotomic character
ideas.modern_name: Weight/cyclotomic character of the motivic Galois group

missed.claim: A 1965 axiomatic list of the structures carried by the motivic Galois group. It covers comparison torsors, Hodge cocharacters, the adelic Galois representation, topological monodromy, π0 compatibility, Frobenius classes and the Tannakian Tate conjecture. This anticipates Serre's 1994 'Propriétés conjecturales des groupes de Galois motiviques' and Deligne's systems of realizations, which are not usually traced back to Grothendieck in this explicit form.
missed.quote: On considère une catégorie de motifs sur K, de type fini, et le groupe de Galois G associé au foncteur de Betti. Cela donne naissance aux structures suivantes.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical attribution: it documents that the programme of conjectural properties of motivic Galois groups was already formulated by Grothendieck in 1965.

missed.claim: Frobenius elements at closed points of a model define Q-rational conjugacy classes in the motivic group G, recovering Weil-type rationality. This is the formulation usually attributed to Serre (1994).
missed.quote: l'élément de Frobenius F_s ... une classe de conjugaison de G (redonne Weil...)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Priority: a central conjecture in the motivic Galois formalism appears here decades earlier.

missed.claim: For K of positive transcendence degree, the motivic Galois group should carry a G_K-invariant absolute integrable connection on the period torsor. Over C this gives a canonical form ω ∈ Ω^1_{C/Q} ⊗ g_Q, linking the motivic Galois group to differential Galois theory of periods over finitely generated fields. It is listed as part of the intrinsic data alongside Galois and Hodge data.
missed.quote: P avec connexion absolue intégrable invariante par G_K ... la connexion absolue définit ω ∈ Ω^1_{C/Q}⊗g_Q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This resonates with relative period conjectures and motivic/differential Galois comparisons (André, Ayoub, Bertrand). Treating ω as a structural invariant of G over transcendental base fields is not a standard part of the formalism.

missed.claim: The page puts topological monodromy of a spread-out model (landing in G(Q)) and the adelic Galois action in one commutative compatibility diagram with π0(G). This anticipates André's theorem that monodromy sits normally inside the motivic/Mumford–Tate group and the Galois-theoretic interpretation of π0.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical precedent for the monodromy-versus-motivic-group comparisons used in André's work and later Hodge-theoretic arithmetic.

deep.surprise_reason: Each individual statement is now standard or conjectural folklore (Serre 1994, Deligne realizations, André). Seeing them assembled by Grothendieck in 1965 as an axiomatic package is a notable historical detail. That package includes Frobenius conjugacy classes in G, the Tannakian Tate conjecture, and a 'groupe de Hodge' contemporaneous with Mumford. The absolute-connection/ω datum for transcendental K is the least familiar ingredient.
transcription_corrections: The top-right box is the group G labelled A (box 'G' with corner 'A'), not '$\boxed{G}_A$' as part of the chain.
Item d) reads roughly 'Pour tout modèle régulier connexe S de K, de type fini sur Z (supposant K de t.f. sur Q)'.
Property 5 reads 'Le composé π1(S,ξ) → G(A) →ε A*, où ε est l'hom défini par [le motif des] racines de l'unité, est l'action de π1(S,ξ) sur les racines de l'unité'.
Property 7 likely reads 'l'élément de Frobenius F_s ... définit dans G(A) une classe de conjugaison de G' (rational conjugacy class), not 'a une classe'.
The item numbered '7)' appears to be overwritten (possibly on an 'F'); the subsequent items are 8 (G_R ... groupe de Hodge) and 9 (Conjecture Tate).
The struck line at the bottom reads approximately 'π1 → G(A) → G(Q_ℓ) → G/G°'.
